item.title: Overcrowding persists at local hospitals
item.description: Overcrowding continues to impact a number of local hospitals. According to the INMO's latest trolley watch report, there were 47 patients waiting for a bed at Sligo University Hospital. This is the fourth highest in the country. Advertisement Elsewhere, there were 6 at Portiuncula Hospital in Ballinasloe and in Mullingar 1. Nationally, University Hospital Limerick remains the most overcowded hospital with 89.

item.title: Body of Liam Farrell to be exhumed
item.description: The body of a man found dead outside his home in county Leitrim is to be exhumed as part of a fresh investigation into his death. RTÉ are reporting Gardaí have obtained permission to exhume the remains of Liam Farrell so that a second post-mortem examination can be carried out. Mr Farrell was discovered outside his house in Rooskey in 2020 and an initial examination concluded that he died from natural causes. item.title: Importance of post offices highlighted locally
item.description: The importance of government support to post offices has been highlighted by a local Councillor. A Dáil debate on Wednesday discussed the closure of post offices. Postmasters previously shared a pot of €30 million in funding in 2022 over three years to help save them from closure. item.description: A civic reception is to be sought for victorious All-Ireland winning Castlerea Community School under 19 basketball team. The west Roscommon school were previously defeated in the under 16 C All-Ireland Schools’ Cup final in 2023. item.title: Litter louts leaving their mark in Ballaghaderreen
item.description: Illegal dumping is now 'completely out of control' in a west Roscommon town. That's according to local councillor Micheál Frain after a large quanity of rubbish was discovered in The Plots area. Residents have previously raised concerns over fly-tipping in so-called 'ghost estates' in the town. item.title: Athlone Town and Shelbourne meet in season opener
item.description: The League of Ireland women’s domestic season gets underway this Sunday with the women’s President’s Cup. Double winners Athlone Town face Shelbourne at the Athlone Town Stadium, kick-off is 2pm. John Sullivan’s Athlone Town will be looking to set the tone early doors for 2026, following last year’s League title & Cup win.
